P1.evidence: The application was read back specifically and early — 'I took a look at your application and got like the basics. 41, you're in tech. Sounds like you're looking to build muscle' — which is the check working as intended. No frame was set at all, and the consequence was immediate and visible: the prospect set the agenda instead. 'So I can give you a little bit of background about myself and like what I've been doing. And then you can probably talk to like how the program works and how you guys can help me.' The rep agreed to that structure, which is why the call ran as an interview followed by a demo rather than a discovery. No agreement question. The open question did run properly: 'in your opinion, what would you say is the biggest challenge that you're having with growing muscle or just your overall fitness right now?'

P2.evidence: Age came from the application rather than the call; height and weight were volunteered inside a longer answer and never asked for. Work was not asked at all until minute twenty-nine, and then assumed rather than asked — the rep said so himself: 'I didn't really even ask, but you're an IT, I assume that's mostly at the desk all day.' Health conditions and injuries were never raised in fifty-three minutes, despite the prospect volunteering 'my shoulders are still sore after doing that' from a self-directed circuit two days earlier. Where the phase was strong it was very strong: the training week was mapped in full detail including honest monthly volume, results and the plateau were established with the specific numbers 204 down to 197-198 and stalled, diet was covered including the 1,400-1,500 kcal intake, and energy was asked directly — 'how do you feel on your day-to-day when you're working or just going about your routine?' Sleep never came up.

P3.evidence: The surface goal was pinned well — 'where are you looking to build muscle on your body?' produced leaner, less flabby, more chiseled, and the rep correctly reframed it off the scale: 'it sounds like for you, it's less about the number and the scale and more about how you look.' The bridge question was asked, and this is the pivotal moment of the call: 'why are you looking to build more muscle now? what's behind that?' The answer was 'I don't have a specific need that I'm looking for.' That is the moment to ask again three different ways, and instead the rep accepted it and moved to diet. Nothing after that reached a driver. Two children and a wife who trains were both on the table and neither was ever used — no 'who else does that impact', no legacy, identity or family thread of any kind. The reflect-back at 00:19:55 was a competent mechanical summary of the three root causes, not the emotional reframe the check asks for. The rep's own verdict afterwards was the same: 'he did not give me enough' and 'I for sure could have went deeper on that.'

P4.evidence: The strongest phase on the call. Past attempts fully mapped — group HIIT classes in 2016-17 with a two-mile run each way, random guided apps, the apartment gym, then Peloton. What happened was quantified: down to 179 lb from 220-230. Why it did not stick was asked and answered honestly: the zero-carb diet was unsustainable and two children arrived. The blocker was named by the prospect himself in precise terms — 'my workouts are all random, and that's why I feel like it is not yielding the results that I'm looking for, even though I'm putting in the effort' — and again as decision fatigue. The rep then ran the right challenge: 'is there any particular reason why you don't just go back to another HIIT class that worked for you before or maybe find some trainer that could work with you in person?', which surfaced that the real constraint is scheduling flexibility around his kids. The only gap is the scripted 'why can't you stick to it on your own', which was implied rather than asked.

P5.evidence: Never ran, and this is the single most consequential omission on the call — the fifth consecutive sales call in this batch where Phase 5 was skipped entirely. The prospect had explicitly stated he has no urgency and feels fantastic. The only route to a cost of inaction was to build one: he has been plateaued for three years, he is 41 and wondering aloud whether it is his metabolism and his age, and he has two young children. 'If nothing changes, where are you in two years?' was the question that would have converted 'I don't have a specific need' into something worth $6,000. It was never asked, so the price landed against a $300-a-month problem.

P6.evidence: A soft temperature check ran before the price — 'as far as that process that we're taking you through, how do you feel about it?' → 'No, I think this is great. I think exactly what I'm looking for' — which is a partial yes and the right side of the sequence. But the belief question was never asked, and the all-in question only ran after the number: 'Outside of that, just having the 6K, is there anything else for you?' The isolation itself was excellent and produced a genuinely useful answer — 'I'm 100% committed. It's just like, I need to figure out how do I bring the funds' — but obtained in the wrong phase it bought certainty about the offer without any leverage behind it.

P11.evidence: Applicable and not done. The prospect stated he was 100% committed and blocked only on funds, which is the exact scenario the deposit policy from eight days earlier was written for. No payment was collected, no deposit asked for, no card taken forward-dated, no payment link sent, no onboarding call with Trevor booked and no agreement mentioned. The call ended with the prospect owning every next action: 'let me talk to my wife and then reach out to you guys back.' The rep's manager identified this precise failure to him forty-five minutes later: 'you're still leaving people without deposits ... you're not going for getting them to actually commit.'

objection_plays.detail: Isolation was the best-executed move on the call and ran twice: 'Outside of that, just having the 6K, is there anything else for you? Is it literally just—' and then the confirmation 'just to be clear, you're not in a place of like, should I do this, but it's just like how to make it?' Both landed cleanly. The financing option was presented. The value reframe ran via the personal-trainer business model, and the prospect actually completed it himself with the expensive-watch metaphor. What did not run is the entire financial picture — not one question about cash on hand, savings balance, credit cards, available credit or investments, despite the prospect twice volunteering that savings exist and that he needs to work out how to access them. Without those numbers there was nothing to build a plan around, which is why the call ended on 'let me figure out how to grab 6K' rather than on a structured arrangement. Credit where due: when asked outright for a discount the rep held the rate and traded duration instead, and then argued against the smaller deal on the prospect's behalf.

Trigger was explicit — 'let me also talk to my wife and see if we can bite into some of the savings'. One move ran, and it ran well: 'is she aware that you have these goals with your fitness?' established that she knows, is supportive, trains herself and might join the programme too. None of the remaining moves ran: no 'money aside, do you personally feel this can get you there', no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger', and no framing of whose decision this is. The scripted fallback — a deposit while he speaks to her — was available under the current deposit policy and was not offered, even though the prospect had already said he was 100% committed.

'Do you like, give me a day of my time to think through it' and later 'let me do a little bit of thinking'. The rep's only probe was 'any thoughts of how you're going to do that over the next day or two?', which asks about mechanics rather than the decision. None of the play ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started'.

notes: Phase 4 was excellent and Phase 3 failed at the one question that mattered. When the prospect answered 'why now' with 'I don't have a specific need', that was the call — everything after it was a well-delivered pitch resting on nothing, which is exactly what the rep and his manager concluded an hour later. Two coachable items beyond the why. First, the deposit: a prospect who says 'I'm 100% committed, I just need to find the funds' is the textbook case for securing something before he leaves, and nothing was secured. Second, the open wallet was skipped entirely — he told you twice that savings exist, and nobody asked how much.
